text: Nothing helps so much to make a prince esteemed as to give signal proofs of his worth, whether by words or by deeds which tend to promote the public good, and show him to be so magnanimous, generous, and just, that he may well pass into a proverb among his subjects.
author: Niccolo Machiavelli
reference: Discourses on the First Decade of Titus Livius
